word_order: SVO — subjects precede verbs and objects follow verbs in examples like "He has been unable to take the drugs".
punctuation_present: always — samples consistently use sentence and clause punctuation (.,;:()"')
register: edited written informational prose (encyclopedic / news / explanatory sentences)
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer emitting segments at sentence-final punctuation and at strong clause boundaries (periods, semicolons, colons, question/exclamation marks). Do not split immediately after prepositions, determiners, auxiliaries, subordinating conjunctions, or tokens listed under unstable_prefix_signals — wait for their complement. Keep closing punctuation and closing quotes/brackets attached to the preceding segment. Avoid splitting at apparent boundaries that are abbreviations, numeric commas, or internal commas in appositions/lists.
